messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — I'm sketching a per-org rate policy that mixes RPM/TPM with a hard concurrency cap. want feedback on two things: (1) how we should surface transient surge probes in the Console, and (2) whether preflight requests should bypass short burst windows.
Kevin Liu: for context: are we talking about preflight like SDK warmups / health checks, or client-side probes (retry probes)?
Maya Patel: both. SDK warmups (prefix caching priming) and internal probes from customers that hammer small requests to test perf. they inflate RPM but not real user work.
Sasha Ivanov: we should treat probe traffic as low-cost but noisy. propose tagging preflight UA patterns and applying a "probe filter" that doesn't decrement burst credits but still counts for telemetry.
Frank Gomez: +1 to tagging, but that leaks complexity to enforcement layer. enforcement currently only knows token/org/key and route. Adding probe exceptions means more rule-matching on the hot path. how expensive is that?
Kevin Liu: it's a couple of string checks and a small whitelist; we can do it at the edge router before routing to runtime. latency impact negligible. main risk is false negatives (legit traffic misclassified).
Maya Patel: UX question: Console should show probe-adjusted and raw RPMs. customers need both. Idea: show a toggle "Hide probe traffic" and store the probe classification rule used for the metric window.
Jen Park: love the toggle. also add a signal: when probe-adjusted throughput diverges >20% from raw, show a tooltip explaining probe rules and suggest adjusting burst window.
Frank Gomez: moving on to concurrency caps — do we apply a per-org hard concurrency limit that always blocks new token execution when exceeded, or a soft cap that queues up to N and then rejects?
Sasha Ivanov: hard cap is simpler for backend stability; soft cap requires queueing policies, memory pressure handling, and fairness. For Dedicated customers we had a soft queue layer, but it caused head-of-line blocking.
Kevin Liu: operationally, hard cap + graceful 429 with Retry-After works best. But we should expose per-route overrides: e.g., model-chat routes might need higher concurrency than embeddings.
Maya Patel: agree. console UX: show live concurrency gauge and a historical heatmap so teams can see when the hard cap would have tripped. Also surface the last 5 rejection samples with example request headers (redacted).
Jen Park: on rollouts — plan: enable hard cap at 90% of observed 95th percentile for a week in read-only mode (no enforcement) and surface an "enforcement ready" checklist. then flip to enforcement with a 5-min grace window for first 24h.
Frank Gomez: what about burst credits? we have a 1-minute burst window currently. If we let probes not consume burst, heavy probe bursts could still cause concurrency pressure. Do we want probe immunity to burst or only to RPM accounting?
Sasha Ivanov: suggest probe immunity only for RPM/TPM accounting. Concurrency and burst tokens should still apply to preserve SLOs.
Maya Patel: ok thats consistent. last: telemetry. We need new metrics: probe_count, probe_adjusted_rpm, enforcement_hits_by_rule, rejected_sample_ids. Add them to per-org dashboard and to Traces for fast triage.
Kevin Liu: I'll add those to the ingestion schema. note: enforcement_hits_by_rule needs cardinality caps — we should bucket by rule_id not full header values.
ratebot: New alert created: org.rate.enforcement_hits > 100/min for 5m -> notify #eng-oncall.
Maya Patel: thanks — can people +1 the rollout checklist here if they agree with the plan?
Sasha Ivanov: +1
Kevin Liu: +1
Frank Gomez: +1
Jen Park: +1
Maya Patel: perfect. I'll draft the PR with the console mockups and updated docs, and a rollout playbook for oncall.
Kevin Liu: ping me on the PR for the edge router changes — I'll review the probe-tag logic.
Maya Patel: noted. closing this thread once PR is up. thanks all :)
